note: The main banks, chosen as the best-known large card issuers (no central bank or banking association ranking was read): Ziraat Bankası, Türkiye İş Bankası and Garanti BBVA. İş Bankası's and Garanti BBVA's fee pages answered not found at the addresses tried, Yapı Kredi's didn't answer and its Worldcard rates page answered not found behind a captcha; a search found Garanti's fees only on comparison sites and in complaints, which aren't sources. Ziraat Bankası's Bankkart rates and fees page, read in full on 2026-10-30 (its rows updated between 15 December 2022 and 9 March 2026): every personal Ziraat credit card is written: the Prestij and Prestij Plus at 1,880 lira a year, the Gold 384, the Classic 222, the Platinum 462 and the Ücretsiz (free) card nothing, each fee including the banking tax (BSMV) where the row says so. Each bears contractual interest of 3.25% a month on a period's debt under 30,000 lira, 3.75% to 180,000 and 4.25% above, the central bank's ceilings (in force from 1 November 2026 at the same figures, read on 2026-10-29); the rate steps with the balance, which the game's card holds as one rate, so the first step is written. Cash advances bear 4.25% a month, and a domestic cash advance costs 1% where the card's rows give it (other banks' ATMs add 2.87% plus 0.57 lira, not written); the default interest (gecikme faizi) of 3.55% a month on a period's debt under 30,000 lira is written as the penalty rate. The page gives no grace period or foreign transaction fee. The youth card (Genç), the Başak producer cards and the business cards aren't written: the youth card's fee is printed as a dash, and the others aren't personal cards. Wave 4 (30 October 2026): Türkiye İş Bankası and Akbank, two of the largest private card issuers, were added because each publishes its full product and service fee table (the form the BDDK requires) at a plain address; Garanti BBVA's fee table, reached at the same kind of address, served only its business and corporate card fees in the page, and Yapı Kredi's answered with a captcha, so neither is written. İş Bankası's product and service fees page (its card fee rows updated 5 January 2026, its rates 1 January 2026), read in full on 30 October 2026: every personal Maximum and Maximiles card with a yearly fee for the main card, each excluding the banking tax (BSMV), whose rate the page doesn't give, so no tax is written: the Visa and Mastercard Classic 1,114 lira, the Gold and Premier 1,303, the Platinum 1,492, the TEMA 1,114, the Olimpiyat 850, Maximiles 1,681, Maximiles Select and Select Mercedes 2,248, Maximiles Black 3,760, Privia Black 5,645 and the Maximum Aidatsız (no-fee) card nothing; the fees are those for cards issued from 2 March 2024 (older cards' may differ, not modelled). The shopping rate is 3.25% a month on a period's debt under 30,000 lira (3.75% to 180,000, 4.25% above: the first step is written, as for Ziraat), the default rate 3.55%, written as the penalty, and cash 4.25% a month; a cash advance through the bank's own channels costs 1% (other banks' machines 2.88% plus 0.58 lira, not written). The student, business, metal, virtual and sticker cards and the North Cyprus (KKTC) rows aren't written. Akbank's product and service fees page, read in full on 30 October 2026 (its card fee rows updated between 28 November 2025 and 8 August 2026, each including BSMV; its rates 1 January 2026): the Axess Classic 1,190 lira a year, Gold 1,329.50, Platinum 1,504.50 and Student 271.50 (for students, a condition the game doesn't check), Wings 1,559.50, Wings Black 2,106 and Wings Elite 9,384. The rate on everything but cash is 3.25% a month on a period's debt under 30,000 lira (stepped as above, the first written), default interest 3.55%, written as the penalty, and cash 4.25% a month; a domestic cash advance at Akbank's channels and other banks' branches costs 1% (other banks' machines 3.87% plus 0.55 lira, not written). Neither bank's page gives a grace period or foreign transaction fee for these cards, so none is written. Akbank's Free card isn't in the fee table and isn't written. The minimum payment is set by the BDDK by the card's limit, the same at every bank: from 3 October 2026, 20% of the period's debt where the customer's limit is 100,000 lira or less and 40% above it (the threshold was 50,000 lira before). İş Bankası's minimum payment page states it for its cards, Akbank's for its cards as the BDDK's rates, and Ziraat Bankası's Bankkart questions page says its minimum is calculated at the rates of the BDDK's Regulation on Bank Cards and Credit Cards (read 2026-10-30; the BDDK's decision itself wasn't reached: its press releases list ends at January 2026 and the official legislation site, mevzuat.gov.tr, didn't answer). A card's limit isn't known before the holder is given it, so every card is written at the least band, 20%, with no floor and no interest on top; a holder whose limit at the bank is above 100,000 lira is asked 40%, which the game doesn't model. İş Bankası's page says a new card takes its limit's band, with no first-year rate.
